settings.editor:
In areas like Springfield, Hendersonville, and White House, spring is the best time to catch small plumbing issues before heavy summer water use puts extra strain on your system.

During summer, plumbing systems work harder than many homeowners realize. Outdoor watering increases, guests come and go, appliances run more often, and small issues that build up over winter can suddenly turn into leaks, clogs, or water heater failures.

At Petitt Heating & Cooling, we see the same pattern every year across Middle Tennessee communities: plumbing problems that could’ve been prevented with a simple spring check.

This checklist walks you through what to look for, what you can safely handle yourself, and when it makes sense to call a professional, so you can head into summer with confidence.

settings.title: Quick Answer: What Should You Check in Your Plumbing Each Spring?

settings.editor: In spring, homeowners should check for leaks, test water pressure, inspect drains, examine exposed pipes, and service the water heater. A simple plumbing check helps catch small issues early and prevent costly repairs as water usage increases in summer.

settings.title: Why Spring Plumbing Checks Matter in Middle Tennessee

settings.editor:
Winter puts quiet stress on your plumbing. Pipes expand and contract, water heaters work harder, and small leaks often go unnoticed. Once temperatures rise, those hidden issues can show up fast.

A spring plumbing check helps you:

  • Catch leaks before they cause water damage
  • Avoid emergency repairs during peak summer demand
  • Improve water pressure and efficiency
  • Extend the life of your plumbing fixtures and appliances
Think of it as a reset after winter and insurance against summer surprises.

Walk through your home and look for signs of leaks, even small ones.

Check:

  • Under sinks and around shutoff valves
  • Behind toilets and at the base of the bowl
  • Around washing machine hoses
  • Outdoor hose bibs and spigots
Slow drips, water stains, or damp areas often mean a small repair is needed before it turns into a bigger problem.

High water pressure feels great, but it can damage pipes, fixtures, and appliances over time.

A few warning signs:

  • Banging or knocking pipes
  • Leaking faucets that won’t stop
  • Appliances wearing out faster than expected
If water pressure feels unusually strong, a professional pressure test can help prevent long-term damage.

Toilets are one of the most common sources of hidden water waste.

Quick test:

  • Add a few drops of food coloring to the tank
  • Wait 15–20 minutes without flushing
  • If color appears in the bowl, the toilet is leaking
This type of leak can waste hundreds of gallons a month, and it’s usually an easy fix.

Spring is a good time to inspect visible plumbing before humidity and heat increase.

Look for:

  • Corrosion or rust
  • Cracks or mineral buildup
  • Pipes that may need insulation in crawl spaces or garages
Addressing small pipe issues now can help prevent leaks or burst lines later in the year.

Rubber hoses wear out faster than many homeowners expect.

What to look for:

  • Bulging or cracking
  • Loose connections
  • Signs of moisture behind the washer
If hoses are more than a few years old, replacing them proactively can prevent major water damage.

settings.title: 6. Flush and Inspect Your Water Heater

settings.editor:
Your water heater works year-round, and spring is a smart time to make sure it’s ready for higher summer use.

Helpful checks:

  • Listen for popping or rumbling sounds
  • Watch for rusty water
  • Look for moisture around the base
Flushing sediment improves efficiency and helps extend the life of the unit, especially important for tank-style water heaters.

settings.title: 7. Test Drains Before Summer Use Increases

settings.editor:
Slow drains don’t fix themselves and summer often makes them worse.

Check:

  • Bathroom sinks and tubs
  • Kitchen sink
  • Shower drains
If water drains slowly or gurgles, it may be time for professional cleaning before a full backup happens.

Spring is when outdoor plumbing gets turned back on.

Be sure to:

  • Check hose bibs for leaks
  • Inspect irrigation lines
  • Look for pooling water in the yard
Outdoor leaks often go unnoticed and waste water. This is especially important for homes in White House and Springfield, where outdoor lines are more exposed to winter temperature swings.

settings.title: 9. Check Garbage Disposal and Kitchen Plumbing

settings.editor:
Run cold water and test your disposal.

Watch for:

  • Unusual noises
  • Slow draining
  • Lingering odors
If something seems off, it’s better to address it now than during summer gatherings or heavier kitchen use.

Some issues are hard to spot without training or tools.

Scheduling a spring plumbing inspection can:

  • Identify hidden leaks
  • Test pressure and expansion tanks
  • Catch early signs of pipe or fixture failure
  • Help prevent emergency repairs during summer
This is especially helpful for older homes or homes with crawl spaces.

settings.title: Frequently Asked Questions About Spring Plumbing Maintenance

items.item_title: Why is spring the best time to check my plumbing?
What plumbing problems are most common in summer?
Should I have my plumbing inspected even if nothing seems wrong?
Can small leaks really lead to major plumbing damage?
How often should homeowners schedule professional plumbing maintenance?

settings.editor: Spring is ideal because plumbing systems are transitioning out of winter stress and into heavier summer use. Small leaks, cracked pipes, and drainage issues often show up during this season, and catching them early helps prevent emergency repairs when water use increases.

The most common summer plumbing issues include leaking outdoor faucets, clogged drains, sewer backups, water heater strain from higher demand, and pipe leaks caused by pressure changes. Many of these start as minor issues in spring.

Yes. Many plumbing problems develop slowly and don’t cause noticeable symptoms until damage has already started. A spring inspection helps identify hidden leaks, pressure problems, or drainage issues before they turn into costly repairs.

Absolutely. Even slow leaks can cause water damage, mold growth, and higher utility bills over time. In crawl spaces and walls—common in Middle Tennessee homes—leaks often go unnoticed until significant damage has occurred.

For most homes, a professional plumbing check once a year is enough to catch developing issues early. Homes with older plumbing, crawl spaces, or frequent drainage problems may benefit from more regular maintenance.
